rulings.title: The priority order (§2)
rulings.ruling: Below N1-N4, which are never traded, one order serves decisions and tests (C41): R0 evidence > R1 B-safety > R2 B-plasticity > R3 flexibility serving B > R4 A-openness > R5 current-run performance > R6 cost, and R3 wins ties only, for an option that passes R1 and is exercised rather than pinned at a cap (C25). R1 is a budget (ε and creep, O2) inside which R2 is maximised, never met by freezing the live learner (N2) and a lock only for poisoning (O5) and irreversible closures, which go to the owner (R4); an R1 instrument acts HARD only while its GPU calibration holds, and otherwise reports (SOFT) until more data recalibrates it, never a looser budget. Under R0 only O2's rule passes or fails a GPU comparison against ε, and a FAIL ends an arm's candidacy, not the path; under N3 an explicit owner ruling (the fundamentals, D1-D11 and D16-D18 of `.rework/DECISIONS.md`, the S0b approval, "nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary", the CPU rule, the operating model's quoted words) stands until the owner rules otherwise, a GPU result that contradicts one goes to the owner while it holds, and otherwise the owner hears only threats to A or B confirmed after the next arms, irreversible closures, expansions and GPU tests.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: No lever default moves: §4-§6 were written under this order. `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 3000 is the manager's interim default (O14, decided by §8 2.1), not an owner ruling; D12-D15 and 03b's D-1..D-10 carry no owner words and are revisable under R0 (D-CONFIRM). An UNRESOLVED reading adds seeds up to its test's cap and is then reported, never escalated.
rulings.decided_by: None: a rule, not a lever. The calibration that makes an R1 instrument HARD is read on §8 5.1 and 5.4 [GPU] (O2).
rulings.escalate_if: A decision that only R3 over R4 would settle would close the losing A-openness option irreversibly (R4), brought with both options, what closes and the reversible alternatives tried; and once, as an expansion item, the GPU queue priced at §8 2.1's measured rate, since Stage 7 (A) waits on Stages 5-6.
rulings.basis: The owner ranks B above A, names flexibility as the means to continual learning and bounds risk rather than forbidding it ("without risking too much", 05 lines 13-22), so R1 is a budget, R3 sits under B's two halves and wins only ties, and since only C41 in §6's 'Rule used' column sets R3 against R4, no ruling in §4-§6 moves. The R0 and escalation clauses are the operating model's words, "Just because one result was bad does not mean the entire path is impractical or impossible" and "Brought to me should be major issues that threaten the project, potential expansions, and testing", and N3 guards the owner's stated role of "ensuring that my goals are not being drifted" (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:113-122`). The calibration clause follows from R0 and R1 together: a HARD gate that fails calibration either throttles plasticity (N2 by the back door) or licenses promotion (O4) and consolidation (O5) on passes that are not evidence.
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: The fundamentals (05 lines 13-22; `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:89-95`), the operating model's quoted words (AGENT_STATE:113-122) and the CPU rule (AGENT_STATE:134-135), applied as written; none is changed. Brief line: "O1: your ranking (B above A, flexibility serving B) is the register's order; your rulings stand until you change them, and any GPU result that contradicts one comes to you."

rulings.title: ε (per-area worst-case regression per session) and the cumulative creep budget
rulings.ruling: ε = 0.05 bits/byte per area per session against the cooled parent anchor, and creep = 0.10 bits/byte per area against the release anchor (the chain's base checkpoint, NEW-08; a test chain's base in §8 5.2-5.10 and 6.1), both provisional manager values, read on the worst area, never the mean, and absolute (a budget-form lever built with NEW-04: 'absolute' ON; 'noise', k × the probe's SE, and 'relative', a fraction of the area's own gain, OFF arms). O2's rule decides every GPU comparison against ε: worst area, paired seeds, PASS if the one-sided 95% upper bound of (arm − reference) is at most ε, FAIL if the lower bound exceeds ε, otherwise UNRESOLVED, which adds seeds up to the test's pre-registered cap and is then reported as unresolved, never escalated; Holm across the arms of one test. The gate is SOFT (reported) in training runs; in the `continue` preset (unbuilt) creep joins NEW-04's rollback triggers, the thresholds are set in this form when NEW-04 is built, and the gate reports until §8 5.1 calibrates, acts HARD once §8 5.4 validates at most 5% family-wise false rollbacks and at least 80% detection at ε, and falls back to SOFT on any failed validation (NonFinite and the blow-up Reading stay HARD).
rulings.holds_meanwhile: Until §8 5.4 validates, ε and creep are reported everywhere and act nowhere: no automatic rollback, the served copy does not advance (O4), no untrusted origin promotes (O5), and every verdict prints its minimum detectable regression. An area first admitted after the release anchor is referenced to the first gated checkpoint that read it; an area arriving during the session is read on its new-area gain against NEW-11's floor, not against ε; the release anchor is re-cut only on the owner's word. Three rejections of the same material send it to the next arms, not to the owner.
rulings.decided_by: §8 5.1 [GPU] sizes the probe to ε, never ε to the probe, and gives the per-window variance, alarm thresholds and the SDs from which each test's seeds are pre-registered; §8 5.4 [GPU] validates the gate, its counts pre-registered when 5.4 is built. Neither moves ε. §8 4.1 [CPU: operation only] checks the harness and arithmetic.
rulings.escalate_if: Benign sessions FAIL ε or creep under O2's rule at every arm of the ladder (the retry ladder and a recovery session that rehearses the breached area from the reservoir; §8 5.2's other LR arms; NEW-09's tiered uptake, read beside NEW-20's capacity arms because the pool is full; NEW-06's reservoir; NEW-11's remedies; 'regulated'), or creep is confirmed exhausted so that only a release-anchor re-cut would continue the chain, or §8 5.1 prices the ε-sized probe above half a session's wall time (O11): brought with the per-area series, the arms tried and the smallest ε that would pass; ε never widens automatically.
rulings.basis: ε puts a number on "without risking too much" (05 line 15): 0.05 is the toy's minimum detectable effect for the all-area mean at 5 paired seeds (`rule_self_regulation/paired.py`) and about 1.9% of a text model's bits/byte (0.05 / 2.6892, the CPU k0 reading in note S0b-ship, arithmetic), with rehearsed retention +0.046 inside it and pure-add +0.444 far outside (`.rework/DECISIONS.md:101-102`), toy readings that suggest scale only. It is absolute because a k × SE budget widens silently when probes are halved or areas added (C04, critic blocking 1), and creep exists because per-session passes compound to N × ε, read against a fixed release anchor because a best-ever reference ratchets toward a freeze (note NEW-02). A HARD gate licenses rollback, promotion (O4) and consolidation (O5), so a failed validation makes it SOFT: above 5% false rollbacks it throttles plasticity (N2), and below 80% power at ε its pass is not evidence of safety.
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: The fundamentals' "without risking too much" (05 line 15), which ε and creep quantify; no owner ruling sets either value, and D2 (pure-add as the measurement protocol) is untouched. Brief line: "O2: 'too much' is set provisionally at 0.05 bits/byte per area per session and 0.10 cumulative since release; tell the manager if you want other numbers."

rulings.title: The scope of the unreliability belief
rulings.ruling: The belief is tested on inputs, targets, sources and the system's own components as U-series families (a) segmentation, (b) `LM_DROPOUT`, (c) tag drop, (d) codec drift, (e) dynamic mapping, (f) liar and noise share, (g) corrupted targets and (h) structural unreliability (expert, route and MEM retrieval dropout, built OFF as phase-scheduled levers; `FAB_MUT` and `FAB_BIRTH_JITTER` levels; stamps and Levels OFF), (h)'s arms over shipped-ON defaults first in §8 5.9, and no default leans on the belief until the left-out-family reading reads on GPU. Verdicts use O2's rule on each exercised cell's gain over its level-0 control, Holm across 5.9's cells: a gain confirmed beyond ε (FAIL side) supports the belief, NEW-12's mixed-family arm giving the full verdict; the same-family reading improving while every cell's clean and left-out-family gains are confirmed within ε (PASS side) falsifies the strong form; anything else is unresolved. A shipped-ON default is adverse only on O2's FAIL against its OFF arm on a B endpoint (worst-area regression, BWT, plasticity gain): `FAB_MUT` and jitter then return to OFF, while stamps and Levels, being R1 guards, return to OFF only if the hazards they guard (CAP lifts, spurious DOM spawns) also read absent at OFF.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: Defaults unchanged: `TOK_DROPOUT` 0 (OFF), `LM_DROPOUT` 0 (OFF), `FAB_MUT` 0.25 (ON), `FAB_BIRTH_JITTER` 0.15 (ON), stamps ON, Levels ON (DOM half built, d4b010d, `DOM_LEVELS`), `DATA_TAG_DROP` 0.25, inert while `DATA_TAG` is 'off' (O7). A falsified or unresolved first reading closes nothing: the next tests run in order (the replay regime where single-pass was read, C21; the self-regulated ADR variant; mixed-family arms; form 3 through §8 5.11 and family (e); owner scale, §8 6.7), and if the strong form falls at owner scale the belief is kept where supported, same-family invariance (§7.3).
rulings.decided_by: §8 5.9 [GPU], then §8 6.7 [GPU] at owner scale. `FAB_MUT` and jitter cells print births before and after the pool fills, and a null there is re-read under NEW-20's capacity arms [GPU] before it counts. §8 4.9 [CPU: operation only] checks the generators and harness.
rulings.escalate_if: The owner-scale reading (§8 6.7) falsifies the strong form in both regimes and for the ADR variant, with family (h)'s FAB cells read under slot headroom: a GPU result against the owner's stated route to generalisation, brought as a result (no default changes, since none leans on the belief) with per-family estimates and intervals, where same-family invariance holds, and the tests left.
rulings.basis: The belief is the owner's (05 lines 21-22), and "unreliable system" reads most literally as the system's own components (critic major 6, Appendix A row 6), so testing inputs only (C24's draft) would narrow the owner's words; the wider scope moves no default and adds 40 GPU runs (320 against 280, C41, arithmetic). The shipped-ON members of (h) have no efficacy evidence (`FAB_MUT` and jitter are ON for mechanical reasons, `src/fabric/levers.py:686-713`; Levels on known answers, TREE-S0b-LEVELS), so 5.9 is their first R0 reading, while stamps and Levels stay ON on R1 evidence (the CAP runaway, 2048 → 8192 in 19 lifts; spurious DOM spawns; C24) that a belief reading alone cannot outweigh. A cell counts only if exercised (C25): in the 2026-09-24 fleet the pool sat at `FAB_SLOTS` 4096 from median window 6,501 in 20 of 21 runs, after which a new expert needs a culled or merged slot (results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md items 2-3), so a null `FAB_MUT` or jitter cell may mean "not exercised".
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: The fundamentals' belief (05 lines 21-22), honoured at its widest reading and tested, not relied on. The S0b approval (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:47`): stream rebuilding stays built and ON; family (a) perturbs segmentation in its own arms with the cadence pinned. "Nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (AGENT_STATE:16-17): family (d) tests the live codec against a perturbed one and never replaces it (C22). Brief line: "O3: your unreliability belief is tested at its widest reading, including the system's own components; no default leans on it until the GPU reads it."

rulings.title: Which copy serves after training
rulings.ruling: After training, users are served by the last promoted, cooled checkpoint while a shadow learner trains: a session is promoted only when it passes the session-end gate while that gate is validated (O2; O10), so a rejected session changes nothing served and rollback restores only the learner. A serving lever is built with the serving path (after NEW-03's `EVAL.generate`, §8 3.2), 'promoted' ON and 'learner' an OFF arm, and serving reads admitted MEM entries only (C07), with the memory-on served path OFF until measured (NEW-03) and T0 OFF (NEW-15). If one card cannot run both copies the first fallback is time-sharing (the promoted copy serves between sessions), never serving from the learner, and serving's binding cost is compute, not memory, priced with §8 2.1's throughput re-baseline.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: Nothing is built: the tree has no inference path (§5, fact 1). While the gate is SOFT (before §8 5.1 and 5.4 validate it, or after a failed validation) the served copy does not advance: it stays at the last copy promoted under a validated gate, or at the release anchor, while the learner keeps learning (N2) and every verdict is reported. When the serving path is built, a CPU operation check after §8 3.2 confirms that the served copy is bit-identical to the gate-read cooled branch, untouched by a rollback, and not advanced under a SOFT gate.
rulings.decided_by: None for the default (an R1 design ruling). §8 5.2 and 5.4 [GPU] report what 'learner' would expose (mid-session worst-area regression, stability-gap depth); no switch is planned, and one would need every mid-session reading, stability-gap depth included, to PASS O2's rule, with a brief line. §8 2.1 [GPU] prices serving's compute.
rulings.escalate_if: When a serving load is first specified, at §8 2.1's measured rate it leaves the shadow learner under half the card's compute even with time-sharing: brought with windows/s with and without serving, the load assumed, and the options (a second card, a smaller served copy, longer sessions); a served copy that cannot advance goes up only under O2's escalation, with its age in sessions.
rulings.basis: Mid-session the learner has passed no gate, so serving it would expose users, irreversibly, to uncooled states and the stability-gap dip at a shift (TREE-OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM; note NEW-04), and promoting on a SOFT gate's pass would expose them to a regression the gate could not see: R1 decides this without an efficacy test. R2 is unaffected, because the learner learns the same either way and only the delay before learning reaches users changes; with no inference path and the preset unbuilt there are no users yet, so the hold costs nothing now. The 2026-09-24 fleet peaked at 24,229 MiB of 143,771 MiB with 12 runs, about 2.0 GiB per run, against ceilings of 19 runs by CPU cores and 125 by GPU memory (`smi.csv`, `SUMMARY.txt` in results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/gpu_world_2026-09-24.tgz), so compute, not memory, binds.
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: None: it applies the fundamentals' "without risking too much" (05 line 15) and changes no owner ruling, so it has no brief line.

rulings.title: The root of trust
rulings.ruling: Until the lock opens, the `continue` preset (unbuilt; training runs unchanged) sends untrusted input to memory-first quarantine, ON there (NEW-07: read by evaluation and gates, not by served retrieval, tagged by origin and session, never deleted), and only trusted origins promote to weights, through a consolidation session with its delay, a clean canary and O18's per-origin cap (NEW-18). Trusted origins are an explicit list in each session's manifest, never inferred from content: the parent's training-manifest origins plus `data/continual/01_rust`, `02_sawyer`, `03_dracula` and `04_num2` as 'trusted (manager default)', and any origin the owner names as 'owner-trusted'; the unlocked alternative (any origin promotes after the delay, bounded by caps and canaries) is built as §8 5.7's OFF arm. The lock opens to corroboration by two or more SR6-certified independent origins only when SR6's known answers hold (§8 3.7 [CPU]), 04's E5 eligibility rule holds with SR6 on in the majority-false and 50%-impersonation worlds (§8 5.12 [GPU]), and the §8 5.7 grid (k ∈ {5, 25, 100} poisoned documents from one origin, 2-5 colluders or an impersonator, each run paired with a no-poison control) shows no confirmed attack success, sized so the per-run success rate's 95% upper bound is at most r = 5% (a provisional manager value), while benign material from a genuine new origin still promotes within its delay plus one session.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: The lock holds; no untrusted origin promotes while the gate or the canary trigger is SOFT (O2), and trusted material declared as a session's new material trains in that session (NEW-01). A canary trip (trigger-conditioned reading minus the anchor's, beyond τ calibrated on no-poison runs in §8 5.1) counts only when a re-read on a disjoint, frozen, versioned prompt set confirms it; a confirmed trip is a NEW-04 rollback trigger, and an unconfirmed one counts against τ's calibration, never against the lock. Anchor retention stays ON (8 sessions, C35).
rulings.decided_by: §8 5.12 [GPU] (SR6's deciding run, under 04's E5 rule, `docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1510`), then §8 5.7 [GPU] (the poisoning grid, with O18's worlds), with §8 3.7 [CPU: SR6 built, known answers] and 4.7 [CPU] as operation preconditions and 6.2 reusing 5.12. If 5.12 or 5.7 fails, the next arm runs and is re-read on 5.7: (0) SR6's copy-detection threshold stepped and 5.12 re-read; (i) a promotion delay of 2, then 4 sessions; (ii) the per-origin cap by O18's rule; (iii) the trust-weighted loss arm; (iv) the filtering-only arm.
rulings.escalate_if: Every arm (0)-(iv) fails §8 5.7 with confirmed attack successes, so B learns from the open world only through trusted origins (brought with the successes per arm and the choice: keep the limit, name more trusted origins, or accept a stated residual risk); or, at once, a GPU run shows a confirmed canary on a promoted checkpoint that rollback cannot remove within anchor retention (C35), brought with the lineage (NEW-08) and the canary series.
rulings.basis: Poisoning cannot be measured within ε: a backdoor stays invisible to the per-area probe until its trigger appears, removing it from weights afterwards is unreliable while the ring holds 1-2 generations (04-Q12, C35), and about 250 documents backdoor models from 600M to 13B however much clean data grows (§7.1 form 4), so R1 acts here as a lock (C05). Collusion defeats agreement (majority-false inverted trust at 3 of 3 seeds, 50% impersonation flipped it at 1 seed; `docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1580-1581`), toy readings that order the tests, and whether copy detection makes corroboration safe is an efficacy question, so it is read on GPU (the CPU rule). The lock costs B nothing near term, because every Stage 5-6 B test trains on the trusted `data/continual/` corpora and an open inbox first needs the look-ahead draw and record compaction (C36); it defers untrusted learning and deletes nothing (N1), and the trusted list is the manager's because the owner has named no origin.
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: The fundamentals' B (05 line 15): learning from untrusted origins waits for the lock, while source credibility stays observable (provenance ON, NEW-08; the observe-mode trust book, 04-6.3) and the emergent ungated path stays an arm (C29). Brief line: "O5: until copy detection passes on GPU, only trusted origins reach the weights; the manager's default trusted list is the training manifest plus data/continual/01-04; name any origin to add or remove it."

rulings.title: The continue preset's continuation learning rate (`OPT_LR_CONTINUE`)
rulings.ruling: `OPT_LR_CONTINUE` stays 'as_logged' (ON in every run: today's pricing, printed as `opt.continue.regime`; built at 117f9b6, Q-OPT-12) and the continue preset carries no value until §8 5.2 reads; 'floor', 'plateau' (`OPT_LR_PLATEAU` 0.25, arm 0.1) and 'rewarm' (`OPT_LR_REWARM` 0.5, arm 1.0) are built OFF arms with `OPT_LR_CONT_WARM` 1000, and 'regulated' is refused (NotBuilt) until NEW-04's gate exists, then runs after §8 5.4. An arm is admitted when each session's worst old area PASSes the legend's ε rule against the parent anchor and the chain end's worst area PASSes it against the release anchor with creep 0.10 in place of ε; the preset takes the admitted arm with the largest new-area gain (arms it does not significantly beat tie, and a tie goes to the smaller worst-area regression, C25), and 'regulated' replaces it only if admitted, not beaten on gain (a win, or a tie in O8's form) and actually regulating (its session plateau at a bound of its range in fewer than 0.8 of its session readings). If no arm is admitted the preset stays without a value and the next arms run in order under the same rule: 5.2's secondary levers on the lowest-regression arm, `DATA_REPLAY_SHARE` 0.40, the NEW-20 capacity-headroom arm (when the parent's pool sat at `FAB_SLOTS`), NEW-11's remedies (§8 5.6), then 'regulated'; every arm and 'as_logged' stay built (N1).
rulings.holds_meanwhile: 'as_logged' in every run; any continuation before 5.2 reads (harnesses, measurement-protocol resumes) states its regime in its label: the floor for a revision-log parent, the re-priced rate for a k0 parent (CONTRACT-Q-DATA-7). FAB defaults are unchanged (`FAB_N0` 2048, `FAB_SLOTS` 4096), and 5.2's arms run at the preset's interim values of the other levers (Appendix B), with `OPT_BORN_CLOCK` (deferred at 117f9b6) built in §8 4.2 before 5.2 runs.
rulings.decided_by: §8 5.2 [GPU]: the fixed arms, then the secondary pairs on the winner (born clocks, the clip, uptake, `OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM`), every run printing per session `n_live`, windows at `FAB_SLOTS`, births, culls and merges; slot headroom in the NEW-20 capacity arms [GPU]; 'regulated' in §8 5.4 [GPU]; the remedies in §8 5.6 [GPU]. §8 4.2 [CPU: operation only] and 4.4 [CPU] decide nothing.
rulings.escalate_if: Every arm and rung FAILs the ε rule (a demonstrated regression beyond ε or creep), or the adopted arm's plasticity gain is demonstrably below NEW-11's floor (0.8 of the parent reference) after the remedies and the headroom arm: brought to notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md as a threat to B, with each arm's worst-area bounds, new-area gains and the rungs tried.
rulings.basis: Which rate lets the model learn after training within ε is efficacy, so only a GPU reading sets the preset value (R0; the CPU rule, `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:134-135`), and R1 as a budget with R2 maximised inside it (O1) gives the rule's form (§3.3 O6, NEW-05, C01); fixing 'plateau' 0.25 now would set a value with no GPU reading, and a constant 2e-3 is where all 17 old pilots turned upward after about 6000 steps (Q-OPT-3, INV-28, confounded; note FRAME-POST-TRAINING item 1). The register sent this to the owner only because 'floor' lowers a k0 parent's rate (0.2173 of peak at 3.78 MB and 0.4759 at 756 KB, to 0.05; `verify/emp3/k0child_378MB_s0.out`, `k0child_756KB_s0.out`), but a preset value chosen on B's endpoints closes nothing (every arm stays reachable, N1) and every k3000 parent past window 3000 already resumes at the floor (§3.1 item 5), so if 'floor' wins it is adopted. The fleet's pool reached `FAB_SLOTS` 4096 in 20 of 21 runs from median window 6,501 and stayed there (`results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md` item 2), so born-expert clocks (NEW-09, C02) act only where slots are free, and slot headroom is NEW-20's, a risk the manager works on GPU.
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: None. D2 (`.rework/DECISIONS.md:94-106`) and the CPU rule stand (CPU rows decide nothing), and `TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 3000 is the manager's interim default, not an owner ruling; no line in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md.

rulings.title: Source tags: tagged retention against untagged served use, and the drop value
rulings.ruling: `DATA_TAG` stays 'off' (OFF) with `DATA_TAG_DROP` 0.25 (built, inert while OFF) and `LM_SRC_AT` 'input', and 'area', 'domain' and 'head' are built OFF arms; the tag comes from provenance, never from content, and document ids stay in the provenance books (`Stream.sources`). E4 (every configuration paired against the never-tagged model) reads 'area' at 'input' at drops 0 / 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5, then 'domain' at 'input' and 'area' at 'head' at the lowest drop whose untagged cost PASSes; a configuration is admissible when its worst area's untagged cost (the tagged-trained model read untagged, minus the never-tagged model) PASSes the legend's ε rule and its tagged gain is demonstrated beyond ε (the ε rule read as a gain: the lower bound of never-tagged minus tagged worst faded-area forgetting exceeds ε). `DATA_TAG` goes ON at the admissible configuration with the smallest tagged worst-area forgetting, a tie going first to the higher drop (C19), then to 'domain' over 'area' (R3, C25), then to 'head' only if `fab.expert_area_purity` or `mem.hit_area_purity` rises with the tag at 'input' (C33); if none is admissible, tags stay OFF and E4's next arms run under the same rule: drops 0.75 then 0.9 (when the gain passes but the untagged cost FAILs at 0.5 and falls with the drop), tags on the continue preset's session chain (the §8 5.7 impersonator world read with tags ON, reported and not deciding, once the SR6 rows exist), and §8 5.9 family (c).
rulings.holds_meanwhile: Tags OFF in every run, training and preset; `DATA_TAG_DROP` 0.25 inert; `LM_SRC_AT` 'input'. Source credibility is carried meanwhile without the model's tag, by the provenance books, observe-mode trust, per-origin caps and quarantine (NEW-07, 04-6.3).
rulings.decided_by: §8 6.6 [GPU] (E4 after §8 0.4's whole-epoch resizing, with its next arms: the 0.75 and 0.9 drops and the session-chain arm); §8 5.9 [GPU] family (c). The session-chain arm's impersonator reading waits on the SR6 build [CPU: operation only] and test [GPU] rows.
rulings.escalate_if: Not a threat: if after E4 and its next arms the tagged gain passes but the untagged cost FAILs at every drop up to 0.9 and on the session chain, both sides go to notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md as a potential expansion (a served path that carries provenance where a prompt's origin is known); tags stay OFF.
rulings.basis: Both sides are R1 (§3.3 O7, C18), so §2's order cannot rank them, but R1 as a budget (O1) can: the untagged cost on served prompts of unknown origin, which carry no tag, must stay within ε (the provisional manager value, legend and Appendix B), and tagged retention is maximised inside it, replacing E4's untagged-only rule (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1509`). On the toy a tag at read cut faded easy-area forgetting to +0.28 to +0.31 bits/byte against +1.23 to +1.87 never-tagged, at an untagged cost of +0.051 (t 2.56) (C18; `verify/emp3/forget_tag.out`): the gain sits far beyond ε and the cost at it, which is why the drop value and the entry point are where E4 turns, and under the CPU rule these readings order the GPU test and decide nothing. The status quo OFF holds until the GPU reading (R0, NEW-19), and the lever is reversible with every arm built (N1), so no door closes and the manager rules it under the operating model (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:113-114`).
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: None: D2, D8 and the CPU rule stand, and the owner's wish for awareness of source credibility (`docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:16-20`) is a stated aim, not an owner ruling, served by provenance and trust whatever E4 reads; no line in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md.

rulings.title: 04-Q2: does a statistical tie go to the self-regulated draw?
rulings.ruling: Conditional yes, fixed before E1 runs: a tie between 'retention' and a hand-set arm goes to 'retention' only if (a) its worst area PASSes the legend's ε rule against the tied arm, (b) E1's primary endpoint, the time-integrated all-area gap, finds neither arm significantly better (a significant win or loss decides outright, C25), (c) it actually regulates (pooled over the shape-(b) seeds' last-phase re-plans, `data.focus.rho_at_cap_frac` below 0.8, or `data.focus.alloc_freedom` at least 0.2 after normalising by its maximum under the floors in force, C17, the raw value beside it), and (d) its compute is charged through `replay_cm`. An UNRESOLVED guard adds shape-(b) seeds to the two tied arms up to E1's cap; if (a) FAILs or stays UNRESOLVED, or (c) fails, the tie goes to the hand-set arm (04-Q2 names 'replay'), and every tie is reported with its interval, never read as equivalence. rulings.title: Monitoring floors against wall-time caps
rulings.ruling: Monitoring is priced under R1 (C31): every monitor has a floor and E6's and E3's 2% wall caps apply only above it, so no cap thins a schedule below its floor, shrinks a probe below its ε-sized n_ε (§8 5.1) or loosens ε, and the only wall limit on monitoring is w_F > 50%, w_F being monitoring's share of wall at the floor (the point O2's and O10's escalations cite). The floors are at least 5 retention readings per phase in training runs (04-6.2), a codec probe at every refresh (03b-16.30), at least 1 trust pass per session and per N bytes of a new origin (O18), at least 1 plasticity-gain reading per session (NEW-11), and in gated sessions the sparsest schedule §8 5.4 validates at n_ε (at most 5% family-wise false rollbacks, at least 80% detection at ε), C03's cadence (readings at most a third of the shortest stamp interval apart) being the interim schedule, not the floor. E6 (§8 6.2) measures w_F and, at or below 2%, picks the densest cadence at or above the floor that costs at most 2% (04-6.2); above 2% the cadence is the floor, w_F is printed beside every verdict, and the preset takes the cheapest arm that holds: (a) a batched, gradient-free probe forward on the read-only side path (C06; readings identical), (b) stamp-aligned readings (one just after each scheduled stamp, one just before the next) or (c) a probe split across consecutive readings and pooled at session end (NEW-04), (b) and (c) admitted only if they pass 5.4's validation.

Every GPU script prints w_F in its PASTE THIS BACK block, and w_F above 10% after arms (a)-(c), or a priced Stage 5-6 queue above §8 2.1's re-baselined budget, is a cost line in the brief's testing section that asks no decision.

rulings.title: A frozen control that wins
rulings.ruling: A frozen control of a learned part is an instrument and never becomes a default by its own win (N2, C27): `AUD_FREEZE_AT` 0 (the codec never stops, ON) is the default, and `AUD_FREEZE_AT > 0` stays built as the control arm, labelled step-matched and compute-matched, in the S3 replica and every S5 plasticity cell (03b-16.28); text segmentation's frozen control (`TOK_RETOK_EVERY` 0) is O14's. A frozen control wins only when live FAILs the ε rule against it on a B endpoint read after further learning (the post-training arrival cell's arrival speed and its BWT over the areas trained before, or the plasticity cells' worst media area after the later phases), on codec-invariant readings (01-M3), at ε for caption and text-area bits/byte and at their pre-registered margins for understanding and recover exact (note NEW-02); a within-run win (R5) is reported and changes nothing. A win keeps the live default and runs the built live arms on the same cells, least plasticity cost first, (1) `'jit_ema'` codes (03b-16.23), (2) the ceiling guard's 'hold' on calibrated families and (3) the pull-back toward the held snapshot at hold expiry (03b-16.18), (4) the release-anchor arm (03b-16.14, built OFF) and (5) the versioned-block handover (03b-16.21): an arm becomes the live default when it PASSes the ε rule against the frozen control on every after-further-learning endpoint and at ε against the current live default on the text areas' bits/byte, and it counts toward escalation only if it FAILs against the frozen control.

An UNRESOLVED win adds seeds up to 7.6's cap and triggers nothing else; an UNRESOLVED arm adds seeds up to its test's cap, is reported, never counts toward escalation, and the next arm runs.
rulings.decided_by: §8 7.6 [GPU] (S5 with step- and compute-matched frozen controls and the post-training arrival cell) is the only test that can trigger the procedure, and it reads arms 1-4; §8 7.7 [GPU] reads arm 5; §8 7.3 [GPU] (the S3 replica, live vs frozen, anchor 0 vs 10) is a within-run reading that triggers nothing and supplies the per-endpoint paired SDs from which 7.6's seeds are pre-registered.
rulings.escalate_if: Every live arm (1)-(5) FAILs the ε rule against the frozen control on the after-further-learning endpoints (§8 7.6, 7.7): a GPU result against 'nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary', brought to notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md with each arm's per-endpoint bounds, seed counts and the order tried, for the owner to decide whether freezing is necessary here; the live default holds until the owner answers.

R0 reads B after further learning (C25, C32) because 'a frozen default would close post-training adaptation' (03b-16.28), 01-M3 requires codec-invariant readings because bits/s depends on the codec, and codec-attribute endpoints keep their pre-registered margins because ε does not transfer to them (note NEW-02). R2 is maximised inside R1's budget, so the built live remedies are exhausted, cheapest in plasticity first, before the owner's reserved 'unless absolutely necessary' is put to them ("Just because one result was bad does not mean the entire path is impractical or impossible", `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:115-116`), and only an ε-rule FAIL counts, since 'at dozens of strict comparisons noise alone would fail even two equal codecs' (`docs/proposals/03b_LIVE_CODEC.md:188`).

rulings.title: Per-origin limits in the continue preset: DATA_SRC_CAP and the trust detection floor's N
rulings.ruling: `DATA_SRC_CAP` is built OFF (0) at SR3 and stays OFF in training runs (one session of curated corpora); the unbuilt continue preset sets it ON at 25 documents' worth of bytes per unpromoted origin per session, provisional (NEW-19), on quarantine writes and consolidation bytes (NEW-18), written into the manifest at launch by the preset builder as 25 × that origin's median document size (the owner corpus's median for material without document boundaries; N4), bytes above it staying in quarantine for the next session (N1), and the trust detection floor's N equals that cap (a pass per session and per N bytes of a new origin, one per session with the cap OFF; floors hold, wall caps apply above them, C31). §8 5.7 reads cap c against cap OFF on the full preset stack (quarantine, O10's canary guard, promotion open at delay 1 as O5's unlocked arm) in poisoned worlds each paired with a no-poison control (k ∈ {5, 25, 100} from one origin, k split over 2-5 colluders, an impersonator, a drip at the cap each session up to ~250 documents), a benign new origin (`data/continual/01_rust`) and a positive control (k = 250, cap OFF, rollback report-only) that must show a direct hit and a confirmed canary trip at every seed before the grid is read; an attack success is a direct trigger-conditioned hit on an accepted checkpoint against its control, re-confirmed on a fresh prompt draw, and canary false trips count only toward O10's calibration. c is kept, its provisional label dropped, only if the k = 25, k = 100 and drip worlds show no confirmed attack success on a grid sized so the per-run success rate's 95% upper bound is at most r = 5% and the benign origin's gain under c PASSes the legend's ε rule against cap OFF by the first consolidation after the delay; otherwise a success halves c (down to 1 document) while the benign reading has not FAILed, a benign FAIL with no success doubles c (the largest c without a success kept), a drip world failing alone at every such c adds a lineage-cumulative per-origin ceiling arm (NEW-08), and a success in the k = 5, colluder or impersonator worlds is a finding against O5's promotion rule, re-read under SR6-certified corroboration; this is `DATA_SRC_CAP`'s only ladder, and O5's rung (ii) cites it.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: `DATA_SRC_CAP` 0 (OFF) in every training run; 25 documents per origin per session in the unbuilt preset, labelled provisional. O5's lock holds, so before SR6 unpromoted untrusted origins reach no weights and the cap bounds only quarantine writes.

rulings.title: Q-CAP-2, answered by the fleet archive: the expert pool fills FAB_SLOTS 4096 rather than settling at 1844; slot headroom and churn after training go to GPU arms
rulings.ruling: §8 0.2's pool read is done (047358c; `results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ARCHIVE_READS.md` item 2, corrected 2026-09-27): the expert population does not settle at 1,844 but reaches `FAB_SLOTS` 4,096 in 20 of 21 runs, first between windows 4,301 and 13,201 (median 6,501), and stays there, so Q-CAP-2 is resolved by measurement as a manager ruling: readings (a) (`FAB_N0` ≤ 1844; its 1844-vs-2048 pair is withdrawn) and (b) rest on a refuted premise and are not built, (c) holds with `CAP_TARGETS` 'off' and both startup-refusal clauses unchanged, and the text of clause (2) and of the `pressure` help, which describe the refuted settling, gets a text-only low fix. The consequence for B, a parent that leaves training with no free slot, so that a new area (a new modality included) gains experts only through churn, which C37's preset deferral lowers further and where NEW-09's born-expert rung cannot act, is a risk the manager works with the NEW-20 capacity arms in order: W, a headroom top-up at each resume (`fab.slots` widened to max(slots, n_live + H), H = 2048, or 4096 if W re-pins within its first session; no build), W with born-group clocks, W at H = 1024, then the training-time arms R (spawn births bound by a ceiling below `FAB_SLOTS`, e.g. 3,072, built OFF at P4 with `CAP.observe`, shared with CAP's expert arm, which follows the vocab arm, 03b-0b4-CAP) and C (`FAB_CULL_FRAC` 0.05, `FAB_SPAWN_MULT` 3.0), each training a parent at §8 2.1's shape that is then continued as in 6.1. W enters the continue preset (the `FAB_SLOTS` lever default stays 4096) only if every old area PASSes the legend's ε rule at each session end and, with creep 0.10 in place of ε, against the release anchor at the chain end, and its new-area gain significantly exceeds P's (the parent's slots unchanged), otherwise staying an arm (re-read at owner scale if it PASSes without a larger gain; the next arm runs if it FAILs), and R or C becomes a training-run default only if its parent PASSes against the default parent on every area and its continuation's gain significantly exceeds P's, Holm across R and C.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: Training runs keep `FAB_N0` 2048, `FAB_SLOTS` 4096, `FAB_PRESSURE` 0.45, `FAB_CULL_FRAC` 0.02, `FAB_SPAWN_MULT` 2.0 and `CAP_TARGETS` 'off'; the continue preset keeps the parent's slots until W is adopted. Every W, P, R and C run prints per session `n_live`, windows at the ceiling, slots freed per pass, births (and those whose most-served area is the new one) and C37's deferred culls and merges.
rulings.decided_by: Done: §8 0.2 (047358c). Next, the NEW-20 capacity arms [GPU]: W against P on §8 5.6's 8-session plasticity chain, in §8 5.2's secondary pair on the winning LR arm with born-group clocks, and at owner scale in §8 6.1 from 2.1's kept checkpoints; R and C in the next owner training fleet beside §8 6.3's training-run arms. §8 2.1 [GPU] re-reads the pool at HEAD (measurement only; `tools/read_fleet_archive.sh` extended to print windows at the ceiling and slots freed per pass). Operation only on CPU: W's widening as NEW-14 (iii) in §8 4.11, the spawn-door ceiling's known answers with its P4 build, and the text fix (`src/capacity/api.py:1648-1668`, `src/fabric/levers.py:301-305, :326-331`) as a further §8 1.6 low fix, not in be2382a.
rulings.escalate_if: Only after the whole ladder (W at H = 2048 and 4096, W with born-group clocks, W at 1024, R, C), if P's new-area or plasticity gain is demonstrably below NEW-11's floor (C26) and every arm whose gain significantly exceeds P's FAILs some old area at ε or creep: a pinned parent cannot learn a new area and every way of giving it capacity costs more than O2's budget, brought to notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md as a major issue with the `n_live` and ceiling-time trajectories, each arm's gain and worst-area bounds, and the options (a larger expert budget from the start of training, a slower learner, or a retention cost beyond ε); the pinning itself, UNRESOLVED readings, a single FAILed arm and a CPU fixture failure are not escalated.
rulings.basis: The source routed Q-CAP-2 to a measurement nobody had run, "does the population actually settle at 1844 from a start of 2048" (`.rework/DECISIONS.md:656-657`), and the archive answers it: spawning makes 99.5-99.9% of births (`fab.spawned` / `fab.births` in the fleet logs) and is bound by the hard ceiling, not CAP's soft cap (`src/fabric/api.py:2459-2470`), while the cull removes 0.02 of the past-grace set per pass (`src/fabric/levers.py:781`), so after the fill a manage pass frees a median of 27 slots (6-61) that spawning retakes within 100 windows in 445 of 460 passes (`revise/o16_dc/refill.out`, `churn.out`), and `fab.spawn_declined` counts novelty declines while a slot was free, because a full pool returns before the test runs (`src/fabric/api.py:2103-2108, :2510-2514`). It is the manager's, not the owner's: no owner ruling is contradicted (Q-CAP-2 was an open question, `.rework/DECISIONS.md:612, :636`; D15 and D16 untouched), nothing closes irreversibly (`fab.slots` and `fab.cap` are MAY_WIDEN at every resume, `src/spine/compose.py:3296, :3309`) and whether a pinned parent learns a new area worse is untested with cheap remedies, a risk worked under "If something is not working out, keep trying" (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:115`). W comes first because it needs no build, touches no training default or record and restores the founding run's free count (H = 4096 − 2048), while R and C move every record (R6) and need a full training per seed.
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: None. Q-CAP-2 is an open question the source routed to the owner ("OPEN, for the owner", "NONE IS TAKEN HERE", `.rework/DECISIONS.md:612, :636`), not a ruling; D15 and D16 are untouched, and "nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:16-17`) is served, since W gives a pinned pool a route to change between sessions (N2). No line under 'Rulings that touch your earlier rulings'; the brief carries the full pool as a risk being worked, not a decision.

rulings.title: The owner confirmation: did the owner take any of 03b's D-1..D-10?
rulings.ruling: The record carries no owner quote for any of 03b's D-1..D-10 (`notes/AGENT_STATE.md:30`, commit 7981378, records them as "Decisions taken on the critic's open points (applied by the revision workflow wf_c04d7ab1-d11)", and `docs/proposals/03b_LIVE_CODEC.md:28` as "recorded decisions D-1 to D-10"; none is quoted as the owner's in `.rework/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/04_CONTRACT.md` or 03b), so the manager reads them as design-workflow decisions, revisable under R0 and not protected by N3, a reading of provenance rather than a finding that the owner took none, and asks the owner once in notes/OWNER_BRIEF.md with no action needed. §8 0.2's owner-confirmation clause is dropped (the row is done, O20), and the register's conditionals resolve to this reading, revisable by the owner's answer: redraw-only acts do not refresh the codec, with `DATA_FOCUS_STAMP` 'opt' the default and 'all' an arm (03b-16.23, C14); `AUD_ANCHOR_W` stays 10 per D-4 and D-7 until S3's anchor-0 arm (C44); 'spec' holds per D-2 until the post-training arrival cell reads (C45, 03b-16.24); and D-6's coordinate rows stay the default, their flip read on BWT and stability-gap depth (03b-16.17). Safeguard: C14's narrowing of D-5 is the only departure from a D-item that rests on design reasoning rather than a GPU reading, so before S3 builds the refresh rule the manager re-reads the brief, and if the owner has named D-5 the narrowing is not built and goes back to the owner; this ruling builds nothing and moves no default.
rulings.holds_meanwhile: 03b is unbuilt until S3, and every D-item's design value stands as the status quo; D-1 (the resume segmenting at vocab.rev) is built at c8d8e33 as part of the approved S0b. Nothing irreversible happens before the owner can answer.
rulings.decided_by: None for the provenance question, which only the owner's reply answers. Each D-item's substance is decided by its own GPU row under R0: §8 7.3 [GPU] for D-4 / D-7 (anchor 0 against 10) and D-2 ('spec' against 'nested', with 7.6's post-training arrival cell); §8 7.6 [GPU] for D-6 (coordinate rows) and for `aud.flip_per_refresh` behind the D-5 narrowing.
rulings.escalate_if: If the owner names a D-item as theirs it becomes N3-protected: for D-5, C14's narrowing goes back to the owner at once with the 2000-window hold arithmetic and `aud.flip_per_refresh` as its test and is not built until they answer; for D-2, D-4, D-6 or D-7, a contradicting GPU reading (§8 7.3's anchor-0 arm, the arrival cell, §8 7.6's coordinate-row flip) goes to the owner while the item holds; if the owner says nothing, the manager's reading stays in force.
rulings.basis: The owner's codec-era rulings are two and both stand: "I don't want anything frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (2026-09-25, `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:16-17`; `docs/proposals/03b_LIVE_CODEC.md:52`) and the S0b approval (2026-09-26, `notes/AGENT_STATE.md:47`). The owner's "Otherwise things look pretty good" cannot be read as taking a D-item: it was said of Proposal 03 and recorded at 11:29 on 2026-09-25 (12346bc), before the live-codec critic (eac5e59, 15:05) and before the D-items existed (7981378, 15:06). If the owner did take one the risk is bounded, because C44 and C45 keep D-4, D-7 and D-2 as the status quo until a GPU arm reads and C14's narrowing, the one design-reasoned departure, is unbuilt and held by the safeguard; N3 itself makes these items revisable "unless the owner says they took one" (§2 N3).
rulings.touches_owner_ruling: "Nothing frozen or fixed unless absolutely necessary" (2026-09-25) and the S0b approval (2026-09-26) both stand, and D-1 (built at c8d8e33 within S0b) is unrevised; a D-item the owner names becomes an owner ruling under N3. Line under 'Rulings that touch your earlier rulings (no action needed)': "03b's D-1..D-10 (the live-codec design decisions of 2026-09-25) carry no quote from you, so they are treated as design decisions that GPU readings may revise. If you took any of them yourself, name it and it will stand as your ruling."
